prompt:
Use case: ui-mockup.
Create one beautiful high fidelity 16:9 GAME DESKTOP OPERATING SYSTEM screenshot concept, the full-screen view entered when the player clicks the CRT computer in a warm pixel-art founder's office. Reference image supplies the game's visual language ONLY: warm cream typography, dark olive charcoal panels, delicate aged-brass rules, pixel-painted details, restrained literary adventure mood. Do not reproduce the office, room inventory, character bust or speech box. This is a diegetic computer desktop, not an external website or SaaS dashboard.
Art direction: bespoke nostalgic late-1990s desktop OS interpreted with the premium cozy pixel-art style of this game. Crisp pixel-edged icons, subtle beveled window chrome, readable compact bitmap/small serif UI type, restrained pale parchment content areas. Wallpaper is an original softly dithered pixel-art landscape of sage hills and an amber dawn sky with lots of quiet dark-green space for icons. Everything is sharp and legible; no heavy scanlines, blur, lens curvature or photographic monitor bezel.
Layout: thin olive desktop menu bar across top, left small emblem and 'WAREWOLF OS', menu labels 'File' 'View' 'Help'; top right 'DAY 01 · 09:00' in the game's refined cream/brass style. Left side vertical four detailed pixel-art desktop shortcuts, comfortably spaced: 'Mail' (envelope with a single unread dot), 'Files' (folder), 'Notes' (notebook), 'Archive' (storage box). These are illustrative app concepts, not a feature roadmap.
One open Mail window near the center-right covering about half the desktop, with title bar 'Mail', small minimize/maximize/close controls, narrow folder sidebar 'Inbox' 'Sent' 'Drafts'. Main pane shows a single selected message and a readable letter:
'Welcome to your new office'
'From: Building Manager'
'Nosh,'
'The keys are yours. Make yourself at home.'
'Good luck with the first day.'
A small 'Reply' button beneath. Keep text short and spacious, no lorem ipsum or tiny illegible paragraphs.
Bottom slim dark olive taskbar with a small 'Start' button, one active Mail tab and tiny sound icon. A clearly legible restrained 'Back to office  ↗' control at far bottom right gives the player a way out of the computer. No mission progress, money, charts, task lists, inventory, RPG meters or dialogue banner. Cohesive interface with breathing room; story-rich but understated. No browser chrome, no watermark, no external brand logos. Render a finished game screen mockup, not a sheet of wireframes.
